.. change::
    :tags: feature, autogenerate

    Added the :paramref:`.EnvironmentContext.configure.table_renames`
    parameter, which accepts an explicit mapping of table names stating that
    a table present in the database has been renamed in the target
    :class:`~sqlalchemy.schema.MetaData`.  Autogenerate then emits an
    :meth:`.Operations.rename_table` directive that preserves the table's
    rows, in place of the drop/add pair it would otherwise produce, with the
    corresponding rename in the downgrade stream.  Each side of the mapping
    may be given either as a plain table name, or as a ``(schema, name)``
    pair for tables in a specific schema.

    The rest of the comparison continues to run against the renamed table, so
    that column, index and constraint differences are still reported, and
    foreign key constraints on other tables that point at the renamed table
    are not reported as changed.  A mapping that cannot be resolved against
    the tables that really exist, such as one whose new name is already
    present in the database alongside the old name, or one that appears to
    point at more than one table in the target metadata, raises
    :class:`.CommandError` before the revision file is generated.

    .. seealso::

        :ref:`autogenerate_table_renames`
